newsitem.title: USA: Video Lottery offered interim aid by Spier.
newsitem.headline: Video Lottery offered interim aid by Spier.

text.p: New York investor William Spier, who has proposed buying Video Lottery Technologies Inc. (VLT) for $6 a share, offered Tuesday to provide interim financial aid to keep the company's subsidiary out of default.

But in a Nov. 26 letter to the company that responds to questions from its board, Spier declined to commit to paying fees for financing commitments before he has received the board's endorsement of his November 15 takeover proposal.
A former Salomon Brothers co-chairman who retired in 1982, Spier is a Video Lottery director who says he holds about 2.5 percent of its stock and heads a group with 14.4 percent.

Spier said "a substantial portion" of the major holders in his investor group would remain passive investors in the new venture. He said he would be the lead investor, which he said was of key importance for obtaining licensing approvals.
Regarding Electronic Data Systems Corp, which has filed suit against Video Lottery on a breach-of-contract claim, Spier said he had no agreement or understanding with EDS.

Still, after discussions "on a conceptual level," he was confident EDS would "work with both VLT and me to remove any obstacles to consummation of my proposal and that EDS' objectives can be met in the context of my acquistion of VLT."
